# ui::Element

Header: `winui/ui/Element.hpp`.

The base of every node in the UI tree: a control, a panel, a window's content.

Implement it: derive a control from it and override the hooks it needs. You call a verb ([measure()](#measure), [arrange()](#arrange), [render()](#render), [tick()](#tick), [handle_key()](#handle_key)) and override its `<verb>_override()`.

Every node measures, arranges, renders, takes input and may take focus. The public verbs apply what is common to all elements (margin, explicit and min/max size, alignment, visibility, requested theme, the visual transform and opacity, animations, the focus ring) and then call the protected `*_override()` hook a control implements. [measure_override()](#measure_override) and [render_override()](#render_override) are required; the rest default to doing nothing. Pointer and key input is routed: the window offers an event to the element under the pointer, or the focused one, and then to each parent until a hook returns true. Containers own their children through `std::unique_ptr` and list them through [for_each_child()](#for_each_child); every tree-wide walk ([tick()](#tick), clear_dirty(), the focus ring, popups, automation) reaches the children through that, so a container overrides it once instead of forwarding each walk. Setters invalidate through [mark_dirty()](#mark_dirty), which bubbles to the root so the window knows to lay out or redraw.

Elements are rendered as a platform-independent command stream ([Renderer](../rendering/renderer.md)), so a control can be measured, arranged, drawn and driven with input without a window or a GPU.

Example: 
```cpp
// A minimal custom control: a color swatch that is clicked with the mouse or Space.
class SwatchControl final : public ui::Element
{
public:
    explicit SwatchControl(ui::Color color) : color_(color) {}

    void set_color(ui::Color color)
    {
        color_ = color;
        mark_dirty(ui::DirtyFlags::Visual); // redraw, no relayout
    }
    void on_click(ui::Callback<void()> handler) { on_click_ = std::move(handler); }

    bool focusable() const override { return true; }

protected:
    bool key_override(const ui::KeyEvent& e) override
    {
        if (e.key != ui::Key::Space)
        {
            return false; // to the parents, the shortcuts and focus moves
        }
        if (e.action == ui::KeyAction::Up && on_click_)
        {
            on_click_();
        }
        return true;
    }
    ui::Size measure_override(ui::Size, const ui::MeasureContext&) const override
    {
        return {32.0f, 32.0f};
    }
    void render_override(ui::Renderer& r, const ui::RenderContext&) const override
    {
        r.fill_rounded_rect(bounds(), 4.0f, color_);
    }
    bool pointer_override(const ui::PointerEvent& e) override
    {
        if (e.action == ui::PointerAction::Down)
        {
            pressed_ = true; // the press holds the pointer until its release
            return true;
        }
        if (e.action == ui::PointerAction::Up)
        {
            // A click is a press and a release, both on the swatch.
            const bool was_pressed = std::exchange(pressed_, false);
            if (was_pressed && bounds().contains(e.position) && on_click_)
            {
                on_click_();
            }
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

private:
    ui::Color            color_;
    bool                 pressed_ = false;
    ui::Callback<void()> on_click_;
};

// In a tree: the panel owns it, the caller keeps an observer.
auto*   panel  = window.set_content(
    std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical));
SwatchControl* swatch = panel->add(std::make_unique<SwatchControl>(ui::Color::from_argb(0xFF0078D4)));
swatch->set_margin(ui::Thickness{4.0f});
swatch->set_horizontal_alignment(ui::Alignment::Center);
swatch->set_tool_tip("Accent blue");
swatch->on_click([] { /* ... */ });
```

## ~Element

```cpp
virtual ~Element()
```

Leaves keyboard focus bookkeeping consistent ([has_focus_within()](#has_focus_within)) when the focused element goes away with its subtree.

## Element

```cpp
Element(const Element&) = delete
```

Not copyable: a control has a parent link, a stable [VisualId](../core/namespace-ui.md#visualid) and its subscriptions, none of which can be duplicated. A derived control is movable until it is parented (the move operations are protected); in a tree it is owned through unique_ptr and never moved.

```cpp
Element& operator=(const Element&) = delete
```

## enabled

## set_enabled

```cpp
void set_enabled(bool enabled)
```

Enables or disables this element and everything inside it. A disabled element draws its disabled look, takes no pointer or keyboard input and leaves the tab ring; so does every element inside a disabled one, whatever its own [enabled()](#enabled). Redraws.

## is_enabled

```cpp
bool is_enabled() const
```

Whether the element takes input right now: its own [enabled()](#enabled), a control's own condition (a [Button](../controls/button.md#uibutton)'s command), and every ancestor's. What a control reads to draw its disabled look.

## focus

```cpp
bool focus()
```

Move keyboard focus here, or, when this element takes no focus itself (a panel, a view's host), to the first focus stop inside it. False, and focus stays where it was, when it is in no window or neither is a stop right now (hidden, disabled). [Window::push_focus()](window.md#push_focus) also remembers what had focus, to give it back.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::TextBox> name;
// ...
name->focus(); // after showing a form, so typing goes into the first field
```

## requested_theme

```cpp
ElementTheme requested_theme() const
```

Measure and draw this subtree in the light or dark version of the theme it is handed ([Theme::with_dark_mode](../themes/theme.md#with_dark_mode)), and so with every color the subtree reads from the theme (background resources, text, control fills). No effect where the theme has no other mode (the fixed-palette eras, high contrast). Tokens the app edited on the handed theme that are not colors (corner radii, type, motion, focus-ring widths) stay as edited; colors are the other mode's. A popup opened from inside is drawn by the window in the window's theme.

## start_animation

```cpp
void start_animation(AnimatedProperty property, Animation animation)
```

Run `animation` on one of this element's visual properties. It replaces whatever runs on any of the same components. A finished [DoubleAnimation](double-animation.md) or [KeyFrameAnimation](key-frame-animation.md) that holds its end (the default) writes its last value into the property, and so does a finished spring. An [ExpressionAnimation](expression-animation.md) runs until [stop_animation()](#stop_animation).


Stop the animation on `property`: the components go back to the property's own value.

## run_transition

```cpp

```

Play `storyboard` on the transition target, replacing one already running; `on_completed` fires once it ends (not when it is replaced), after the target is back at identity. An empty storyboard has nothing to play: it resets the target and calls `on_completed` at once, inside this call.

## add_subscription

```cpp
void add_subscription(Subscription subscription)
```

Take ownership of a [Subscription](../core/subscription.md) so that its lifetime is exactly this node's lifetime. The tree is single-owner and destroyed hierarchically, so a node's subscriptions die with it and a [Property](../core/property.md) can never dispatch into freed memory. A [Property](../core/property.md) dying first is handled inside [Subscription](../core/subscription.md) itself (core/Property.hpp).

Called by the spec layer's [build()](spec-vocabulary.md#build) for every reactive field; an app writing imperatively may call it directly to tie a hand-made observer to a node's lifetime.

## subscription_count

```cpp
std::size_t subscription_count() const
```

How many bindings this node holds: a spec that binds N fields produces N subscriptions. Nothing in the framework branches on it.

## clear_subscriptions

```cpp
void clear_subscriptions()
```

Drop every binding on this node, leaving whatever values were last written in place. Call it to stop tracking the bound properties and drive the control by hand from then on.

## add_shortcut

```cpp
void add_shortcut(Shortcut shortcut)
```

Add a shortcut scoped to this element. [Window](window.md) offers every key press to the shortcuts of the focused element and then of each of its ancestors, innermost first, before the focused element's own [handle_key()](#handle_key) sees it, so a [Tabs](../controls/tabs.md#uitabs) control's Ctrl+T works wherever focus is inside it. A shortcut added here only fires while focus is in its element.

## handle_shortcut

```cpp
virtual bool handle_shortcut(const KeyEvent& e)
```

Offers `e` to this element's shortcuts; true when one handled it. Controls with keys of their own that must work from anywhere inside them ([Tabs](../controls/tabs.md#uitabs) control's Ctrl+Tab) override this, calling the base first.

## handle_global_shortcut

```cpp
virtual bool handle_global_shortcut(const KeyEvent& e)
```

The shortcuts that fire wherever focus is. The ones a command surface carries are of this kind (a [MenuBar](../controls/menu-bar.md#uimenubar)'s Ctrl+S, a [MenuFlyout](../controls/menu-flyout.md#uimenuflyout) item's Delete, an [AppBarButton](../controls/app-bar-button.md#uiappbarbutton)'s Ctrl+N), so those controls answer here. [Window](window.md) offers a key that no scoped shortcut took to every element in the window, in tree order, when the focused element and its parents did not handle the key themselves ([key_override()](#key_override)). Default: none.

## set_tool_tip

```cpp
void set_tool_tip(std::string text)
```

A plain-text tool tip on any element. [Window](window.md) shows it beside the pointer once the pointer has rested on the element for 800 ms, and hides it on a click, a key or the pointer moving off. [ToolTip](../controls/tool-tip.md#uitooltip) (ui/dialogs/ToolTip.hpp) stays the way to give a tip arbitrary content or its own placement.

## tool_tip_at

```cpp
virtual std::string tool_tip_at(Point p) const
```

The tip for window point `p`, which [Window](window.md) asks for as the pointer moves: [tool_tip()](#tool_tip) unless the control shows a different tip per part (a [TableView](../controls/table-view.md#uitableview) cell). A change of text while the pointer stays on the control closes the open tip and starts the wait again.

## cursor_at

```cpp
virtual std::optional<CursorShape> cursor_at(Point) const
```

The control's own cursor at `p` (window-client DIPs, inside [bounds()](#bounds)) when [set_cursor()](#set_cursor) has set none: IBeam over a [TextBox](../controls/text-box.md#uitextbox)'s text, Hand over a hyperlink, a resize arrow over a splitter. nullopt (the default) leaves it to the ancestors. [Window](window.md) asks the innermost element under the pointer first, then each parent in turn, and the first answer wins.

## automation_valid


## automation_children

```cpp
virtual void automation_children(std::vector<Element*>& out) const
```

The children an automation client sees under this node, immediate children only. A client walks the tree one level at a time, and the parent comes from [parent()](#parent). Defaults to every child [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) lists. Override it only to show a client something else: the children in a different order, or without parts that are only decoration. A composite that is one automation node lists nothing.

## automation_focus

```cpp
virtual Element* automation_focus() const
```

While this element has keyboard focus, the node inside it that has it as automation sees it: the row, tab or menu item a control moves its own cursor over with the arrow keys. Screen readers announce that node. nullptr (the default) is this element itself.

## automation_is_native_host

```cpp
virtual bool automation_is_native_host() const
```

True only for [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol) (ui/hosting/NativeControl.hpp). Its child HWND answers automation clients itself, so the automation tree (ui/AutomationTree.hpp) leaves it out and treats it as childless, which keeps it from being described twice.

## automation_parent_of

```cpp
virtual Element* automation_parent_of(const Element& child) const
```

The automation node between this element and its child `child`, for a container whose automation tree has a level its element tree lacks (a table's cell around a template cell the table owns). nullptr, the default, makes this element the child's automation parent.

## measure

```cpp
Size measure(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const
```

Measure the desired size within `available`. Unbounded (+infinity) on an axis means no limit; 0 is no room. The result is always finite. Applies the margin and the size limits, then calls [measure_override()](#measure_override) for the control-specific work. Subclasses implement that hook and don't override [measure()](#measure). Asked again with the same size, measurer and theme while nothing at or below the element was marked DirtyFlags::Measure, it returns what it returned last time without calling [measure_override()](#measure_override): a [measure_override()](#measure_override) must depend on nothing else, or [invalidate_measure()](#invalidate_measure) whenever that something changes. The context's measurer and theme must outlive the next [measure()](#measure): a virtualizing container re-measures from [arrange()](#arrange) and [render()](#render) with the ones it was last measured with.

## measure

```cpp
Size measure(Size available, const TextMeasurer& measurer, const Theme& theme = Theme::default_light()) const
```

[measure()](#measure) with a context of `measurer` and `theme`, for measuring a control on its own. The theme defaults to [Theme::default_light()](../themes/theme.md#default_light), as [render()](#render)'s does.

## parallel_measure_safe

```cpp
virtual bool parallel_measure_safe() const
```

Whether this element's [measure()](#measure) may run on a layout worker thread while its siblings are measured on others ([ParallelLayout](parallel-layout.md)). Default false, so an element nobody checked is always measured on the UI thread.

Answer true only when [measure_override()](#measure_override) touches nothing but this element's own state, the children it lists in [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) (each of which answers for itself), the measurer and the theme: it builds no children, reads or writes no [Property](../core/property.md), subscribes to nothing, invalidates nothing, and uses no cache or static shared with other elements. A part it measures without listing it in [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) makes the answer false. The answer is inherited, so a subclass whose [measure_override()](#measure_override) does more overrides it back.

## arrange

```cpp
void arrange(const Rect& final_rect)
```

Place the element at its final position and size within `final_rect`. Applies margin and alignment, then calls [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) to position any children. The default [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) does nothing, since most leaves need only [`bounds()`](#bounds). [measure()](#measure) is always called before [arrange()](#arrange). Given the rect it was last given, with nothing at or below it measured or marked DirtyFlags::Arrange since, it does nothing.

## bounds

```cpp
const Rect& bounds() const
```

The rect the last [arrange()](#arrange) gave this element, in window-client DIPs (not relative to the parent), after margin and alignment; excludes the margin. Empty before the first layout, and zero-sized while Collapsed.

## hit_region

```cpp
virtual HitRegion hit_region(Point p) const
```

Classify `p` (window-client DIPs, inside [bounds()](#bounds)) for [Window::hit_region_at()](window.md#hit_region_at). Each element answers for its whole subtree. The default passes the question to the topmost child under the point, of those [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) lists, and answers Client where there is none, so an ordinary tree is Client everywhere and only a subtree that opts in drags the window. [TitleBarControl](../controls/title-bar.md#uititlebarcontrol) answers Caption for its own background. [DragAreaControl](../controls/drag-area.md#uidragareacontrol) answers Caption for everything but the focusable controls inside it.

## title_bar_drag_region

```cpp
std::optional<bool> title_bar_drag_region() const
```

Whether a press on this element, inside a [TitleBar](../controls/title-bar.md#uititlebar)'s content, drags the window. nullopt (the default) lets the [TitleBar](../controls/title-bar.md#uititlebar) decide: an enabled focusable control takes the press, anything else drags. true drags even over a control (and, on a container, lets its controls drag too unless they say false). false never drags, over this element or anything inside it. Read on every hit test, so a change takes effect at once.

## set_title_bar_drag_region

```cpp
void set_title_bar_drag_region(std::optional<bool> value)
```

Sets or clears (nullopt) the drag-region override; read by the next hit test.

## render

```cpp
void render(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const
```

Draw this element: nothing while Collapsed or fully transparent, else [render_override()](#render_override) through the visual transform and opacity ([visual_transform()](#visual_transform), [current_opacity()](#current_opacity) times the transition target's). Emits no extra command for an element whose visual layer is at rest, so a still tree renders exactly what [render_override()](#render_override) alone would. A container draws each child through this, handing on the context it got.

## render

```cpp
void render(Renderer& renderer, const Theme& theme = Theme::default_light()) const
```

Draw this element under `theme` ([Theme::default_light()](../themes/theme.md#default_light) by default): a control drawn on its own, or the root of a tree.

## handle_pointer

```cpp
bool handle_pointer(const PointerEvent& e)
```

Deliver a pointer event to this element and everything inside it. It is hit-tested once: the topmost Visible, hit-test visible ([is_hit_test_visible()](#is_hit_test_visible)) and enabled element under the pointer gets it in [pointer_override()](#pointer_override), with its position mapped into that element's layout coordinates (through every [visual_transform()](#visual_transform) and [map_to_children()](#map_to_children) on the way), then each parent up to this one, until one returns true. A press that something handled captures the pointer for that element and its parents until the release, so they get the moves and the release wherever the pointer goes. An element the pointer moves off gets a Leave (once the capture is over, if it holds it), and [on_pointer_entered()](#on_pointer_entered)/on_pointer_exited() are raised. [Window](window.md) calls this on its content; a test can call it on any element, which then routes within its own subtree. Returns whether an element handled the event.

## on_pointer_entered

```cpp
void on_pointer_entered(Callback<void()> handler)
```

The handler for the pointer moving onto or off this element (a press holds neither back; the pointer leaving the window exits). Hit where the element is drawn, as its input is.

## on_pointer_exited

```cpp
void on_pointer_exited(Callback<void()> handler)
```

The handler for the pointer leaving the element; see [on_pointer_entered()](#on_pointer_entered).

## on_got_focus

```cpp
void on_got_focus(Callback<void()> handler)
```

The handler for keyboard focus arriving on this element, or on anything inside it, from outside it. Moving focus between two elements inside it raises nothing here. [Window](window.md) raises it once the focused element has been told (set_focused()).

## on_lost_focus

```cpp
void on_lost_focus(Callback<void()> handler)
```

The handler for keyboard focus leaving this element and everything inside it; see [on_got_focus()](#on_got_focus).

## handle_wheel

```cpp
bool handle_wheel(const PointerEvent& e)
```

A wheel turn, which [Window](window.md) routes through this instead of [handle_pointer()](#handle_pointer): hit-tested like a pointer event, offered to the element under the pointer in [wheel_override()](#wheel_override) and then to each parent until one returns true, so the innermost scrollable region under the pointer scrolls and the page behind it does not. Returns whether an element reacted to it.

## handle_key

```cpp
bool handle_key(const KeyEvent& e)
```

A key press or release. [Window](window.md) delivers it to the focused element and then to each parent in turn until one handles it; what nothing handles goes on to the shortcuts, a dialog's default button and arrow-key focus moves. Offers a press to [on_key_down()](#on_key_down) first, then calls [key_override()](#key_override); true when either took it.

## on_key_down

```cpp
void on_key_down(Callback<Handling(const KeyEvent&)> handler)
```

The handler for a key pressed (or repeating) while focus is on this element or inside it, for app code: an Escape that closes a view, arrow keys that page through it. It sees the key before this element's own handling and after that of the elements inside it that have focus. [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops the key there; [ui::NotHandled](../core/namespace-ui.md#nothandled), or returning nothing, lets it go on to this element and then to the ones around it. One handler per element; setting another replaces it.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> details_open{true};
auto               view = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
view->on_key_down([&](const ui::KeyEvent& e) {
    if (e.key != ui::Key::Escape) return ui::NotHandled;
    details_open = false;
    return ui::Handled;
});
```

## on_wheel

```cpp
void on_wheel(Callback<Handling(const PointerEvent&)> handler)
```

The handler for a wheel turn over this element or one inside it, for app code: Ctrl+wheel to zoom. It sees the turn before this element scrolls and after the elements inside it under the pointer had theirs; `e.position` is in this element's coordinates, and `e.wheel_delta` is positive when the wheel turns toward the user (scroll down). [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops the turn there; [ui::NotHandled](../core/namespace-ui.md#nothandled), or returning nothing, lets it go on. One handler per element; setting another replaces it.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<float> zoom{1.0f};
auto                tiles = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
tiles->on_wheel([&](const ui::PointerEvent& e) {
    if (!e.modifiers.ctrl) return ui::NotHandled;
    zoom = std::clamp(zoom.get() + (e.wheel_delta < 0 ? 0.1f : -0.1f), 0.5f, 3.0f); // up zooms in
    return ui::Handled;
});
```

## raise_wheel

```cpp
bool raise_wheel(const PointerEvent& e)
```

Offers a wheel turn to [on_wheel()](#on_wheel), then to [wheel_override()](#wheel_override); true when either took it. What the wheel dispatch calls for each element under the pointer.

## handle_text

```cpp
bool handle_text(const TextInputEvent& e)
```

Typed text, routed like a key (focused element first, then its parents). Calls [text_override()](#text_override) and returns its answer.

## handle_text

```cpp
bool handle_text(std::string_view text)
```

[handle_text()](#handle_text) with the text alone.

## focusable

```cpp
virtual bool focusable() const
```

Whether this element can take keyboard focus (a leaf control opts in).

## takes_tab_key

```cpp
virtual bool takes_tab_key() const
```

Whether [Tab](../controls/tabs.md#uitab) and Shift+Tab reach this element while it has focus, instead of moving focus (a text box that indents). Ctrl+Tab never moves focus either way. Default: false.

## take_menu_access

```cpp
virtual bool take_menu_access(char32_t letter)
```

Alt or F10 alone (`letter` 0), or Alt with a letter nothing else used, asks for the menus. The window offers it to each visible, enabled element in tree order until one takes it: a menu bar takes keyboard focus (and opens the menu whose header starts with `letter`) and returns true. Default: false.

## is_focused

```cpp
bool is_focused() const
```

Whether this element has keyboard focus: the window's focused element, or a part a composite control draws as focused on its behalf (a [ComboBox](../controls/combo-box.md#uicombobox)'s text field). Kept by the window.

## takes_focus_at

```cpp
virtual bool takes_focus_at(Point p) const
```

Whether a press at `p` (window DIPs) gives this focusable element focus. [Window](window.md) asks it of every stop in the ring and focuses the innermost that says yes, so a stop inside another wins. The default is the whole of [bounds()](#bounds); a control that is one stop for only part of what it covers answers for that part, or a press on non-focusable space inside the rest would focus it ([NavigationShell](../controls/navigation-shell.md#uinavigationshell): its menu, not the page it hosts).

## focus_visible

```cpp
bool focus_visible() const
```

Whether a focused element draws its focus ring: true when the keyboard moved focus, false after a click gave it. [Window](window.md) writes it; a control checks it next to its own focused state when it renders. True by default, so a control focused without a [Window](window.md) draws its ring.

## has_focus_within

```cpp
bool has_focus_within() const
```

Whether keyboard focus is on this element or on one inside it. A repeater checks it before clearing an element (a focused element stays realized). Kept by [Window](window.md) through [note_keyboard_focus()](#note_keyboard_focus); an element destroyed while focused takes its part of the count with it.

## note_keyboard_focus

```cpp
void note_keyboard_focus(bool focused)
```

[Window](window.md)'s side of [has_focus_within()](#has_focus_within): this element gained or lost keyboard focus.

## collect_focusables

```cpp
virtual void collect_focusables(std::vector<Element*>& out)
```

Append focusable elements in tab order, so the [Window](window.md) can build a flat focus ring over the whole tree. The default pushes this element when [focusable()](#focusable), then recurses into every child [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) lists. Override it when the ring differs from the children: a composite that is one tab stop pushes only itself, a focus scope stops recursing (see [collect_scope_focusables()](#collect_scope_focusables)), a pager leaves out its hidden pages.

## selection_group

```cpp
virtual const void* selection_group() const
```

The set of choices this control is one of, or nullptr (the default). Focusable controls that return the same pointer act as one group for the keyboard: [Tab](../controls/tabs.md#uitab) stops once on the group, on the member whose [SelectionItemProvider](selection-item-provider.md) says it is selected, or else the first. The arrow keys move between the members in tree order, wrapping, and select the one they reach ([SelectionItemProvider::select_item()](selection-item-provider.md#select_item)). Ctrl+arrow only moves. Automation clients see each member's position in the set. A [RadioButton](../controls/radio-button.md#uiradiobutton) bound with [ui::selects()](../core/namespace-ui.md#selects) returns the property it was bound to.

## default_focus

```cpp
virtual Element* default_focus()
```

The element [Window](window.md) focuses when this becomes the open modal, or nullptr for the first stop in its tab ring. [DialogControl](../controls/dialog.md#uidialogcontrol) picks something in its content first, else its default button.

## focus_scope

```cpp
bool focus_scope() const
```

Whether this element is a focus scope. By default a container adds its focusable descendants to the window's one flat tab ring ([collect_focusables()](#collect_focusables)), so [Tab](../controls/tabs.md#uitab) walks the whole tree leaf by leaf. A focus scope is one tab stop instead. Enter steps into it, [Tab](../controls/tabs.md#uitab) then cycles only its own inner ring, and Escape steps back out onto the container ([Window::enter_focus_scope()](window.md#enter_focus_scope) and exit_focus_scope()). A navigation pane of fifteen collapsible groups that are scopes is fifteen [Tab](../controls/tabs.md#uitab) stops wide instead of eighty.

Off by default, and set per instance: the same [Expander](../layout/expander.md#uiexpander) can be a grouping box in one layout and a navigable group in another. A control can serve as a scope only if it overrides [collect_scope_focusables()](#collect_scope_focusables) (and [scope_step()](#scope_step) for scopes that navigate items). Setting the flag on a control that overrides neither has no effect, since [Window](window.md) doesn't enter a scope with an empty inner ring.

## set_focus_scope

```cpp
void set_focus_scope(bool scope)
```

Makes this element a focus scope (or an ordinary, transparent container again); redraws.

## bring_into_view

```cpp
void bring_into_view()
```

Ask every scrolling ancestor to reveal this element, innermost first. [Window](window.md) calls it whenever focus lands somewhere, because a tab ring that walks into a scrolled-off region would otherwise park focus on something the user cannot see.

## start_bring_into_view

```cpp
void start_bring_into_view(const BringIntoViewOptions& options = {})
```

Ask every scrolling ancestor to reveal this element (or `options.target_rect` of it), placed as the options say. Unlike [bring_into_view()](#bring_into_view) the whole element is revealed, focus ring or not, and whatever [bring_into_view_area()](#bring_into_view_area) says.

## effective_viewport

```cpp
Rect effective_viewport() const
```

What the scrolling ancestors (and the window itself, the root's bounds) leave in view around this element, in arranged coordinates, not clipped to the element's own bounds. Empty when an ancestor shows nothing; a huge rect when nothing above the element clips it at all (an element with no parent).

## caret_bounds

```cpp
virtual std::optional<Rect> caret_bounds() const
```

Where text typed into this element goes, while it has focus: the caret, in arranged coordinates, or nullopt when it takes no text. The platform puts an input method's candidate window and the emoji panel there ([Window::caret_bounds()](window.md#caret_bounds)). A control that hands its typing to an inner text box answers with that box's.

## bring_into_view_area

```cpp
virtual std::optional<Rect> bring_into_view_area() const
```

What [bring_into_view()](#bring_into_view) reveals when focus lands here (arranged coordinates), or nullopt to leave every scrolling ancestor where it is. The element decides, the scroller follows.

Override it when the whole element is not what should come into view. A grid that draws all its cards itself has bounds as tall as its content, so revealing them jumps the viewport to the top on every focus gain; it answers with the current card's rect instead, or nullopt when there is none.

## reveal_child

```cpp
virtual Rect reveal_child(const Rect& area, const BringIntoViewOptions& options)
```

Reveal `area` (arranged coordinates) and return where it sits after scrolling, so the next ancestor up works with the new position. That makes a scroller nested in a scroller work without a layout pass in between. `options` places it ([start_bring_into_view()](#start_bring_into_view)); [bring_into_view()](#bring_into_view) passes the defaults, the smallest scroll. Default: nothing to reveal, geometry unchanged. [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll) is the only override.

## scroll_info

```cpp
virtual std::optional<ScrollInfo> scroll_info() const
```

This element's scrolling, or nullopt for one that does not scroll (the default). [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll), VirtualList and [ListView](../controls/list-view.md#uilistview) answer.

## parent

```cpp
Element* parent() const
```

The container this element sits in (non-owning), or nullptr for a root or an element not yet added anywhere.

## for_each_child

```cpp
virtual void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const
```

Call `visit` once for each child this element owns, in order (back to front where they overlap). The one override a container needs beyond measure, arrange and render. The default of every tree-wide walk recurses through it ([collect_focusables()](#collect_focusables), the popup walk, clear_dirty(), [build_visual_tree()](#build_visual_tree), sync_composition(), [sync_native()](#sync_native), [tick()](#tick) and [automation_children()](#automation_children)), so a custom container that lists its children here gets focus, popups, dirty clearing, ticks, composition, native controls and automation right without forwarding any of them. Default: no children, a leaf.

List the children the walks should reach, normally every one this element owns. A walk that must see a different set overrides that walk alone: a composite that is one tab stop and one automation node, a split view leaving its closed pane out of focus and popups. A control that parks parts (an unselected page, a hidden button) may leave them out here instead and clear them in [clear_dirty_override()](#clear_dirty_override) (and tick them in [tick_override()](#tick_override)), so a parked part never stays dirty.

Const so the const walks can use it, though it hands out mutable children: they are owned objects of their own, not part of this element's state. A tick can run a handler that adds or removes children, so a container that allows that walks its list by index.

Example: 
```cpp
class Row : public ui::Element
{
    void for_each_child(ui::ChildVisitor visit) const override
    {
        for (const auto& child : children_)
        {
            visit(*child);
        }
    }

    std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ui::Element>> children_;
};
```

## is_dirty

```cpp
bool is_dirty(DirtyFlags flags = DirtyFlags::All) const
```

Whether any of `flags` is set on this node, for this node or, since flags bubble up, for something below it. A new element starts fully dirty.

## dirty_flags

```cpp
DirtyFlags dirty_flags() const
```

Every dirty flag currently set on this node.

## on_screen

```cpp
bool on_screen() const
```

Whether the last frame the [Window](window.md) measured drew some of this element inside the client area: false once it is scrolled out of view, clipped away, collapsed, fully transparent or no longer drawn at all. Only an element that called [set_screen_tracking()](#set_screen_tracking) is told; for any other element, and for one no frame has measured yet, this is true.

## on_screen_changed

```cpp
virtual void on_screen_changed(bool on_screen)
```

Called after a frame in which [on_screen()](#on_screen) changed, for an element that called [set_screen_tracking()](#set_screen_tracking). The frame that brings an element back into view calls it with true, so a control that paused its clock off screen restarts it here ([request_tick_in()](#request_tick_in) works from it). The default does nothing.

## tick

```cpp
void tick(Duration delta)
```

What [Window::tick()](window.md#tick) calls on the root with the time elapsed since the last tick. Elements never read a clock themselves. Advances this element's own animations and transitions (its visual layer), runs [tick_override()](#tick_override), then ticks every child [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) lists. Not virtual, so the children are always ticked. A handler run by the tick may remove elements. They are kept alive until the tick returns, and a child removed before its turn is skipped.

## sync_native

```cpp
virtual void sync_native(NativeHost& host)
```

Called by [Window](window.md) after layout/input changes, with sync_composition()'s cadence. The default only recurses into the children ([for_each_child()](#for_each_child)); [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol) (winui/ui/hosting/NativeControl.hpp) overrides it to place its child window.

## sync_spell_checker

```cpp
virtual void sync_spell_checker(SpellChecker&)
```

Hands the focused element the spell checker. This is not called tree-wide. [Window](window.md) calls it from set_focus(), right before set_focused(true), and before every key or character, so a field is checked the moment it gains focus. A field keeps the pointer after losing focus (its squiggles stay, and it still re-checks when the checker's generation() moves on). A field that was never focused is never checked. [TextBox](../controls/text-box.md#uitextbox) overrides it. Composites with an internal [TextBox](../controls/text-box.md#uitextbox) (ComboBox/NumberBox/AutoSuggestBox) do not forward it, since none of them hold prose.

## handle_context_menu

```cpp
virtual bool handle_context_menu(std::optional<Point>, ContextMenuHost&)
```

Window::handle_context_menu() calls this on the focused element when the user right-clicks or presses Shift+F10/the Menu key, after focusing whatever focusable element sits under the pointer, as a pointer Down would. `position` is the right-click point (window-client DIPs), or nullopt for a keyboard request, where the element picks its own anchor ([TextBox](../controls/text-box.md#uitextbox): its caret). `host` is only valid for this call, so show a menu through it here or not at all. Returns whether a menu was shown; default: none.

## on_context_requested

```cpp
void on_context_requested(Callback<Handling(std::optional<Point>)> handler)
```

The handler for a right-click, Shift+F10 or the Menu key on this element or one inside it. For a right-click [Window](window.md) asks the innermost element under the pointer and then each ancestor, focusable or not; then, and for the keys, the focused element and each ancestor, innermost first, ahead of [handle_context_menu()](#handle_context_menu). The handler is the target asked to act: unless it returns [ui::NotHandled](../core/namespace-ui.md#nothandled) it has shown something (a [MenuFlyout](../controls/menu-flyout.md#uimenuflyout)'s show_at(), a [CommandBarFlyout](../controls/command-bar-flyout.md#uicommandbarflyout)) and the request goes no further. `position` is as [handle_context_menu()](#handle_context_menu)'s. One handler per element; setting another replaces it.

## raise_context_requested

```cpp
virtual bool raise_context_requested(std::optional<Point> position)
```

Runs the handler set above, if any; whether it took the request. A wrapper that stands in for the element it wraps in the tab ring (a flyout around its anchor) asks that element too.

## allow_drop

```cpp
bool allow_drop() const
```

Whether this element is a drop target, getting [drag_enter()](#drag_enter)/drag_over()/drag_leave()/drop() while a drag ([DragDrop::start()](drag-drop.md#start)) is over it.

## set_allow_drop

```cpp
void set_allow_drop(bool allow)
```

Makes the element a drop target (or not); takes effect for the next drag movement.

## drag_enter

```cpp
virtual void drag_enter(const DragEventArgs& e)
```

The drop events. [drag_over()](#drag_over) is asked first on the innermost drop target under the pointer, then on its drop targets up the tree until one accepts; every element asked has heard [drag_enter()](#drag_enter) first and hears [drag_leave()](#drag_leave) once the drag is no longer its business. The one that accepted gets [drop()](#drop). A control overrides them; the defaults run the handlers set with [on_drag_enter()](#on_drag_enter)/on_drag_over()/on_drag_leave()/on_drop().

[drag_enter()](#drag_enter): the drag has come over this element; [drag_over()](#drag_over) follows at once.

## drag_over

```cpp
virtual DragResponse drag_over(const DragEventArgs& e)
```

The drag is over this element: answer what a drop here would do. Asked when it arrives and at every move. The default runs the [on_drag_over()](#on_drag_over) handler, and refuses without one.

## drag_leave

```cpp
virtual void drag_leave(const DragEventArgs& e)
```

The drag left this element, was canceled over it, or was dropped on another target.

## drop

```cpp
virtual void drop(const DragEventArgs& e)
```

The pointer was released over this element while its [drag_over()](#drag_over) accepted. What the drop did is the operation it accepted.

## on_drag_enter

```cpp
void on_drag_enter(Callback<void(const DragEventArgs&)> handler)
```

The handler the default [drag_enter()](#drag_enter) runs; one per element, setting another replaces it.

## on_drag_over

```cpp
void on_drag_over(Callback<DragResponse(const DragEventArgs&)> handler)
```

The handler the default [drag_over()](#drag_over) runs, which answers for the element.

## on_drag_leave

```cpp
void on_drag_leave(Callback<void(const DragEventArgs&)> handler)
```

The handler the default [drag_leave()](#drag_leave) runs.

## on_drop

```cpp
void on_drop(Callback<void(const DragEventArgs&)> handler)
```

The handler the default [drop()](#drop) runs.

## drag_completed

```cpp
virtual void drag_completed(DataPackageOperation result)
```

A drag this element started has ended. `result` is what the target did (None when the drag was canceled or dropped nowhere).

## transition_opacity

```cpp
virtual float transition_opacity() const
```

How far this element's own open or close fade has come, 0 (hidden) to 1 (fully shown), as for a [Flyout](../controls/flyout.md#uiflyout)'s open and close fade or a [DialogControl](../controls/dialog.md#uidialogcontrol)'s open fade. The control advances it in [tick_override()](#tick_override). The window draws everything the element shows at this opacity: a popup owner's floating content, or a modal's scrim together with its content, so one fade covers both. Default 1: fully visible, no fade running.

## build_visual_tree

```cpp
void build_visual_tree(VisualTree& tree, VisualId parent_id) const
```

Add this node, every child [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) lists under it, and then what [build_visual_tree_override()](#build_visual_tree_override) adds, into `tree` under `parent_id` (InvalidVisualId for the root). Called by [Window::layout()](window.md#layout) after [arrange()](#arrange), so [`bounds()`](#bounds) reflects the just-computed layout. Not virtual, so the children are always reached.

## raise_context_requested_in

```cpp
static bool raise_context_requested_in(Element& root, std::optional<Point> position)
```

A context request inside a subtree that is not in the tab ring (an item's content, drawn by an items control that is the one tab stop): raised on the innermost visual child of `root` under `position` (or on `root` for a keyboard request) and bubbled to `root`. Returns whether a handler took it.

## Element

```cpp
Element() = default
```

Constructs an element with a [visual_id()](#visual_id) of its own, fully dirty and in no tree.

## automation_providers

```cpp
virtual void automation_providers(AutomationProviders& out)
```

Lists what a client can do with this node: set `out`'s field for each pattern this control implements now to `this`, through the provider interface it inherits privately (ui/Automation.hpp). A pattern that only applies in some states is an `if`. `out` arrives empty, and nothing is listed by default.

Example: 
```cpp
class Chip final : public ui::Element, private ui::InvokeProvider
{
protected:
    void automation_providers(ui::AutomationProviders& out) override
    {
        out.invoke = this;
    }

private:
    bool invoke() override
    {
        on_click_();
        return true;
    }
    ui::Callback<void()> on_click_;
};
```

## open_popup

```cpp
void open_popup(PopupRequest request)
```

Floats `request.content` above the tree, hung from `request.anchor` (this element by default), or updates the popup this element has open. Each element has at most one popup; a control that shows several uses several elements. The window places it after every layout, draws it with its shadow over everything else, routes input inside it to it alone, and on a press outside it or Escape calls `request.on_dismiss`. It closes with [close_popup()](#close_popup) or when this element is destroyed. Calling it again while open, from [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) for an anchor that moves, lays the popup out again only when something other than the callbacks changed.

## close_popup

```cpp
void close_popup()
```

Closes the popup [open_popup()](#open_popup) opened. Nothing when none is open.

## popup_open

```cpp
bool popup_open() const noexcept
```

Whether this element has a popup open.

## Element

```cpp
Element(Element&& other) noexcept
```

Moves a not-yet-parented element (a factory returning a control by value); see the copy operations' comment. Never move an element that is already in a tree (asserted). The new element gets a [visual_id()](#visual_id) of its own and starts fully dirty; the [ElementWatch](element-watch.md) objects on the source follow it here. What the moved-from element is left with is only fit to be destroyed.

## operator=

```cpp
Element& operator=(Element&&) = delete
```

Deleted: an element has an identity (its visual id, the watches on it, the handlers that captured it), so assigning one over another has no sensible meaning.

## measure_override

```cpp
virtual Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const = 0
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](#measure) and [arrange()](#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete Element must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](#bounds) set, which the base already did.

## arrange_override

```cpp
virtual void arrange_override(const Rect&, const ArrangeContext&)
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

## render_override

```cpp
virtual void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const = 0
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

## pointer_override

```cpp
virtual bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e)
```

A pointer event for this element: the element under the pointer, one inside it that did not handle the event, or the element holding the capture. The position is in layout coordinates ([handle_pointer()](#handle_pointer)). Return true when the event did something here, and it goes no further up; a handled press also captures the pointer until its release. A control that acts on a press (a click, a toggle, a caret placed, a drag started) returns true for the press and its release, so a list row or a card around it does not act on the same click. Default: false.

## handled_pointer_override

```cpp
virtual void handled_pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e)
```

A pointer event that an element inside this one handled (its [pointer_override()](#pointer_override) returned true), so it never reached this element's [pointer_override()](#pointer_override). Called on each element above the one that handled it, innermost first, with the position in this element's layout coordinates. A container that has to see every press inside it, handled or not, overrides it: a swipe that may turn a press on a button into a drag, a table that commits an open edit when a check box in another row is pressed. Default: nothing.

## wheel_override

```cpp
virtual bool wheel_override(const PointerEvent& e)
```

A wheel turn over this element ([handle_wheel()](#handle_wheel)). Return true when it scrolled something here. Default: an element with no children hands it to [pointer_override()](#pointer_override) and returns false; one with children returns false.

## hit_test_children

```cpp
virtual void hit_test_children(Point p, std::vector<Element*>& out) const
```

The children `p` (in this element's layout coordinates) is tested against, topmost first. Default: what [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) lists, last first. A container that draws in another order ([Panel](../layout/panel.md#uipanel)'s z-index), a control with parts [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) does not list, or one whose parts cover others in places (a pane drawn over the content) lists them here.

## map_to_children

```cpp
virtual Point map_to_children(Point p) const
```

A point in this element's layout coordinates, mapped into its children's: a control that scrolls, zooms or scales its content maps it the way the content is drawn. Default: the point unchanged.

## children_hit_clip

```cpp
virtual std::optional<Rect> children_hit_clip() const
```

Where the children can be hit, in this element's layout coordinates, or nullopt for anywhere (the default): a scrolling control returns its viewport, so content scrolled out of view is not hit.

## hit_test_transparent

```cpp
virtual bool hit_test_transparent() const
```

Whether the pointer passes through this element and everything in it to what is behind, as if it were not there: a wrapper with nothing visible in it ([ContentHost](../controls/content-host.md#uicontenthost) while its child is missing or collapsed). Default: false, so an element is hit anywhere in its bounds.

## covers_children_at

```cpp
virtual bool covers_children_at(Point p) const
```

Whether a part of this element drawn over its children is at `p` (a scroll bar over the content), so the element is hit there instead of a child. Default: false.

## capture_pointer

```cpp
void capture_pointer()
```

Capture the pointer of the event being handled: keep receiving its events, wherever it goes, until [release_pointer()](#release_pointer) or the release of the button. A handled press does this by itself. Only while handling a pointer event.

## release_pointer

```cpp
void release_pointer()
```

End a [capture_pointer()](#capture_pointer) or the capture a press took.

## tick_override

```cpp
virtual void tick_override(Duration delta)
```

This element's own part of [tick()](#tick): a clock of its own ([ToolTip](../controls/tool-tip.md#uitooltip)'s hover delay, an animation's phase, a caret blink). Runs after the visual layer has advanced and before the children are ticked, which [tick()](#tick) does by itself. Tick only parts that [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) does not list here. Default: nothing.

## clear_dirty_override

```cpp
virtual void clear_dirty_override(DirtyFlags flags)
```

This element's own part of clear_dirty(): clear any part it owns but leaves out of [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) (a parked page, a hidden button), through that part's clear_dirty(). Default: nothing.

## build_visual_tree_override

```cpp
virtual void build_visual_tree_override(VisualTree& tree) const
```

This element's own part of [build_visual_tree()](#build_visual_tree): add any part it owns but leaves out of [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) through that part's build_visual_tree(tree, visual_id()). Default: nothing.

## collect_scope_focusables

```cpp
virtual void collect_scope_focusables(std::vector<Element*>&)
```

The inner tab ring, built when this scope is entered: a scope's counterpart to [collect_focusables()](#collect_focusables). A container that becomes a scope must stop recursing in [collect_focusables()](#collect_focusables) and recurse here instead ([Expander](../layout/expander.md#uiexpander) is the worked example), since a child in both rings would be reachable without ever entering.

Three meaningful answers:
- several elements: an ordinary container scope. [Tab](../controls/tabs.md#uitab) cycles them, Escape leaves.
- `this` alone: an item-navigating scope. The control's items are not all elements ([ListView](../controls/list-view.md#uilistview) creates its rows on demand and destroys them as they scroll out), so focus stays on the control and [Tab](../controls/tabs.md#uitab) is routed to [scope_step()](#scope_step) below.
- nothing: there is nothing inside worth entering. [Window](window.md) doesn't enter, and the key that would have entered goes to this element's own [handle_key()](#handle_key). That is how Enter expands a collapsed [Expander](../layout/expander.md#uiexpander) that is marked as a scope.

The one walk that does not default to recursing through [for_each_child()](#for_each_child): being a scope is something a control opts into, and a default inner ring would make every container enterable while its children still sat in the outer ring too.

## scope_step

```cpp
virtual bool scope_step(int)
```

Move an item-navigating scope's own inner cursor one step: `delta` is +1 for [Tab](../controls/tabs.md#uitab) and -1 for Shift+Tab. Wrap and return true to keep focus inside the scope (Escape is then the way out, as for an ordinary container scope). Return false to let the step fall out, popping the scope and leaving focus on this control. Never called for a scope whose inner ring is real elements, since [Window](window.md) walks that ring itself.

## set_scope_entered

```cpp
virtual void set_scope_entered(bool)
```

Called by [Window](window.md) as this scope is entered (before its inner ring takes focus) and again as it is left, so a control can show and hide whatever inner cursor it draws. A container scope whose inner ring is real Elements usually needs nothing here, since the focused child draws its own focus ring, as it would anywhere else.

## take_focus_request

```cpp
virtual FocusRequest take_focus_request()
```

For a part of the main tree that takes focus when it opens, as [SidePane](../layout/side-pane.md#uisidepane)'s light-dismissable pane does. It holds the tab ring while open (by answering [collect_focusables()](#collect_focusables) with the pane alone) and hands focus back when it closes. Returning a request consumes it; the default never asks. Escape reaches it like any key the focused element inside it leaves alone ([key_override()](#key_override)).

## focus_request_root

```cpp
virtual Element* focus_request_root()
```

The subtree an Enter request focuses into; `this` by default.

## draws_focus_ring

```cpp
virtual bool draws_focus_ring() const
```

Whether the window draws this element's focus ring while it is [focusable()](#focusable), [is_focused()](#is_focused) and [focus_visible()](#focus_visible). True by default, so a focusable control gets the ring by doing nothing. The window draws it after everything else in the window, or in the popup the element is in, clipped only by the scrolling viewports around the element, and layout never makes room for it. The theme decides its shape and whether it sits just outside or just inside [focus_ring_rect()](#focus_ring_rect). Return false only for a control that shows focus in a shape of its own (a text field's accent border) or not at all.

## focus_ring_rect

```cpp
virtual Rect focus_ring_rect(const Theme& theme) const
```

What the ring goes around, in window DIPs: [bounds()](#bounds) by default. A control whose ring goes around one part of it (a slider's thumb, a list's current row) returns that part. `theme` is the one the element is drawn with, for a ring placed differently per theme.

## focus_ring_inside

```cpp
virtual bool focus_ring_inside() const
```

Whether the ring goes inside [focus_ring_rect()](#focus_ring_rect) in every era, its outer edge on the rect. False by default, which leaves it to the theme. An item inside a viewport (a list row, a tab, a menu item) returns true, as does a control in a tight spot, so a neighbor or the viewport edge never cuts its ring.

## focus_ring_corner_radius

```cpp
virtual float focus_ring_corner_radius(const Theme& theme) const
```

The ring's corner radius: the theme's control radius by default.

## key_override

```cpp
virtual bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e)
```

A key for this element: the focused one, or one inside it that did not handle it. Return true when the key did something here, and it goes no further; false lets it bubble on to the parent and then to the shortcuts, a dialog's default button and arrow-key focus moves. Default: false.

## text_override

```cpp
virtual bool text_override(const TextInputEvent& e)
```

Typed text for this element, routed like [key_override()](#key_override). Default: false.

## focus_changed

```cpp
virtual void focus_changed(bool focused)
```

Keyboard focus arrived (true) or left (false); [is_focused()](#is_focused) already says so. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

## focus_visible_changed

```cpp
virtual void focus_visible_changed(bool visible)
```

[focus_visible()](#focus_visible) changed; the element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

## enabled_changed

```cpp
virtual void enabled_changed()
```

[is_enabled()](#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

## set_enabled_gate

```cpp
void set_enabled_gate(bool open)
```

A condition of the control's own that is ANDed into [is_enabled()](#is_enabled) (a [Button](../controls/button.md#uibutton) whose command may not run). True by default.

## attached

```cpp
virtual void attached()
```

The element joined a window's tree: [window()](#window) is now that window. Called for the root a window takes and for everything inside it, and for a subtree added to a tree already in a window. No-op by default.

## detached

```cpp
virtual void detached()
```

The element left a window's tree (moved out of it). No-op by default.

## automation_name_fallback

```cpp
virtual std::string automation_name_fallback() const
```

[automation_name()](#automation_name)'s fallback when [accessibility()](#accessibility).name is empty. Default: no inherent name, correct for controls with no visible text of their own ([Slider](../controls/slider.md#uislider), [ProgressBar](../controls/progress-bar.md#uiprogressbar)), which need an explicit [accessibility()](#accessibility).name from the caller. A control with its own visible text ([Button](../controls/button.md#uibutton), [CheckBox](../controls/check-box.md#uicheckbox), [TextControl](../controls/text.md#uitextcontrol), ...) overrides this to return it.

## automation_help_text_fallback

```cpp
virtual std::string automation_help_text_fallback() const
```

[automation_help_text()](#automation_help_text)'s fallback when [accessibility()](#accessibility).description is empty. Default: none. An input with a `description` under it returns that text, or its `error` while set.

## automation_invalid

```cpp
virtual bool automation_invalid() const
```

True while the control holds input it reports as wrong (an input's `error` is set); screen readers say so. Default: false.

## mark_dirty

```cpp
void mark_dirty(DirtyFlags flags, std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
```

Mark this node dirty and bubble the newly set bits up the parent chain, so an ancestor's flags show that something below it changed without walking the subtree. Bubbling stops at the first ancestor that already has the bit, since every ancestor of a dirty node is dirty in the same way.

Every setter goes through here, so this is where a build with thread checks catches a setter called on an element under a [Window](window.md) from another thread than the window's. Leave `where` defaulted: it names the setter that called this.

## invalidate_measure

```cpp
void invalidate_measure(std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
```

This element's size has to be measured again (and it arranged again): [mark_dirty()](#mark_dirty) with DirtyFlags::Layout. For a setter whose value changes the element's desired size.

## invalidate_arrange

```cpp
void invalidate_arrange(std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
```

This element has to be arranged again, its size has not changed: [mark_dirty()](#mark_dirty) with DirtyFlags::Arrange. For a setter that only moves the element or its children within the space they already have (an alignment, a scroll position that is laid out).

## request_tick

```cpp
void request_tick()
```

Keep the window ticking: for an element that waits for time to pass without changing anything in the meantime (a caret between blinks, a delay before something opens). A window stops ticking a few seconds after its last tick that changed something, so a longer quiet wait calls this from [tick_override()](#tick_override) for as long as it lasts. A wait of known length is cheaper with [request_tick_in()](#request_tick_in).

## request_tick_in

```cpp
void request_tick_in(Duration delay)
```

Have the window tick again `delay` from now (0 or less: at once), for an element whose next change has a known time (the next frame of an animated image). Unlike [request_tick()](#request_tick) it does not keep the window busy: an otherwise idle window sleeps until then and wakes only for it ([Window::next_wake()](window.md#next_wake)). Call it from [tick_override()](#tick_override) or [on_screen_changed()](#on_screen_changed). It holds for one tick, so an element that still waits asks again from its next [tick_override()](#tick_override), which may come sooner. A hidden or minimized window does not wake for it.

What the same [tick_override()](#tick_override) changes with [mark_dirty()](#mark_dirty) is that step's change (a caret blink, an image's next frame): it is drawn, and it does not make the window busy either. A [tick_override()](#tick_override) that also animates something calls [request_tick()](#request_tick) as well, or the window waits for the requested time before its next tick.

## set_screen_tracking

```cpp
void set_screen_tracking(bool on)
```

Have the [Window](window.md) report [on_screen()](#on_screen) for this element and call [on_screen_changed()](#on_screen_changed) when it changes, from the frames it measures from now on. Off by default, and free while off. A control turns it on while its drawing moves on its own (an animated image), to pause while nobody can see it. Turning it off makes [on_screen()](#on_screen) true again.

## check_thread

```cpp
void check_thread(std::source_location where = std::source_location::current()) const
```

[mark_dirty()](#mark_dirty)'s thread check without the dirtying, for a setter that changes nothing drawn (an event handler, a tip): reports a call from another thread than the one of the [Window](window.md) this element is under. Leave `where` defaulted: it names the setter that called this.

## note_child_deleted

```cpp
void note_child_deleted()
```

For a container whose child just started an [AddRemoveTransition](element-transitions.md#struct-addremovetransition) exit. In the next arrange the children it moves close the gap only once that exit has played, and a child added in the same pass fades in after them, so neither slides over the one still leaving. A [RepositionTransition](element-transitions.md#struct-repositiontransition) on those children gives way to it for that pass.

## desired_content_size

```cpp
Size desired_content_size() const
```

What the last measure asked for, without the margin: how large the content is, where [bounds()](#bounds) may be the larger slot a stretching parent gave it.

## set_parent_of

```cpp
static void set_parent_of(Element& part, Element* parent)
```

Record [`parent`](#parent) as the container `part` sits in (nullptr: none), when a container adds a child or a part of its own. Dirty flags bubble up this link, and the new parent chain takes on the part's dirty flags and keyboard focus ([has_focus_within()](#has_focus_within)) while the old one lets go of the focus, so a container that adopts a dirty part is laid out again without marking itself. Not an ownership transfer: the container already holds the part's unique_ptr.

## clear_dirty_of

```cpp
static void clear_dirty_of(Element& part, DirtyFlags flags = DirtyFlags::All)
```

Clear `flags` on `part` and its subtree, for a [clear_dirty_override()](#clear_dirty_override) clearing a part this element leaves out of [for_each_child()](#for_each_child).

## set_focused_of

```cpp
static void set_focused_of(Element& part, bool focused)
```

Show `part` focused or not, for a composite that draws one of its parts as focused while it holds the focus itself (a [ComboBox](../controls/combo-box.md#uicombobox)'s text field). Hand [focus_visible()](#focus_visible) on with [set_focus_visible_of()](#set_focus_visible_of) too, or the part keeps drawing its ring after a click.

## set_focus_visible_of

```cpp
static void set_focus_visible_of(Element& part, bool visible)
```

Hand the focus-visible state on to a part; see [set_focused_of()](#set_focused_of).

## key_handled

```cpp
static bool key_handled(const KeyEvent& e, bool arrow, bool enter, bool shortcut)
```

The usual answer for a focused control's [key_override()](#key_override): an arrow when `arrow` (the control uses that arrow), Enter when `enter`, a shortcut-like key (Ctrl, Alt, Delete, Insert, a function key) when `shortcut`, never [Tab](../controls/tabs.md#uitab) or Escape, and any other key (typing, Space, Home, PageDown) always, since a focused control owns its plain keys.

## struct ScrollInfo

What a scrolling element tells something that follows its scrolling, such as a [Parallax](../layout/parallax.md#uiparallax).

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `offset` | `Point` |  | how far the view is scrolled into the content (zoomed DIPs) |
| `viewport` | `Size` |  | the view's size |
| `extent` | `Size` |  | the content's size, unzoomed |
| `zoom` | `float` | `1.0f` | the zoom factor; 1 unzoomed |
| `out_of_bounds_pan` | `Size` |  | How far past either end the content can be pulled: a tenth of the viewport for a plain scroller, a whole viewport for a zoomable one. |
| `content` | `const Element*` | `nullptr` | The element that is the content, whose top-left is the content's origin; nullptr when the content is not one element (a list's realized rows). |
